requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request implementation source.

- **Syntactic-ancestry segments.**
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`, `extern[C]/fn[puts]`, and duplicate names as `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`. It also checks that each selector resolves back to the same node and that the ambiguous `fn[repeated]` is rejected.
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` repeats the main cases.
- **No cross-file module resolution.** `functions_in_a_separate_module_file_are_selected_within_that_file` outlines `lib.rs` with `mod local;` and `local.rs` with `pub fn run() {}`. It asserts that the declaring file yields only `mod[local]` and that the module file yields exactly `fn[run]`, with no `mod[local]` segment.
- **Required outline node kinds.**
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts functions, methods (in both inherent and trait impls), `struct[Thing]`, `enum[E]`, `union[U]`, traits, impls, `mod`, `macro[make]` (a `macro_rules!` definition), `const[C]`, `static[S]`, `type[Alias]`, and extern blocks.
  - That test also covers `extern-crate[core]`, `type[Item]` inside a trait, and `extern[Rust]` for a block with no ABI.
- **Impl naming.**
  - `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]` are asserted.
  - `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` is asserted for a non-path self type.
  - `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` for a generic impl.
- **Anonymous items.**
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` asserts that `use` declarations get `use@…` selectors and that two different `use` items get distinct selectors.
  - `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts that item-position macro invocations match `^macro@[0-9a-f]{12}$` and are distinct. It also asserts that nested ones appear under their ancestor, for example `impl[...]/macro@…`. Macros inside function bodies produce no nodes, which the node count of 7 confirms.
- **Documented spelling.** `every_profile_mapping_is_documented` checks that `md/reference.md` contains the selector spellings: `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`, `extern[C]/fn[puts]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`, and `use@3f2a9c01b7de`. It also checks the anonymity sentence and "Modules are never resolved across files.", and that every Rust profile mapping appears in the profile table.

I found no plausible violating behavior that these tests would accept, and there are no acknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline, except
that a Markdown profile MAY additionally recognize colon-fenced directive
containers under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`
and expose them as outline nodes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. Such containers MUST
preserve source ranges and containment, and MUST NOT be recognized within
literal code or raw HTML. Other nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline
descendants appear under the nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
